messages:
marta_support: FYI customer Acme is seeing a big surge -> lots of 429s and 1.5s tail latency during a marketing pulse. They say dedicated pool didn't spin up in time. attaching logs from their request timeframe.

devon_oncall: ack, can you paste the sample request IDs + time window? Also any repro steps from them?

marta_support: timestamps ~ 2025-11-03T21:03:10Z to 21:07:35Z. Example req id: req_0a3f. Customer sent a 50rps fanout ramp over 90s. Their config: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=24, scale_policy=queue_length with target=150. They expected autoscaler to add capacity after queue > 150.

sam_runtime: quick snapshot from our metrics during that window: queue_length peaked ~ 420, pending_provision_count=6, scale_latency_ms (controller->provision) median 38s, p95 92s. Provisioned nodes appeared but remained NotReady for another ~40s (image pull + warmup). So end-to-end from threshold->serving ~120s.

alex_infra: that aligns with a quota bump throttling event on the cloud side around 21:04 — our provision requests were rate-limited for ~30s. opsbot: "Provision request rate-limited by cloud-provider (429)" (automated alert).

lia_csm: customer expects <30s for scale to meet burst. They have a business SLA for marketing spikes. We need mitigation and a short-term fix.

devon_oncall: repro steps to simulate locally: run a burst script against dedicated endpoint with controlled ramp:
```
for i in {1..50}; do seq 1 100 | xargs -n1 -P50 curl -s -X POST https://dedicated.acme.redwood/api/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'; sleep 0.5; done
```
This should recreate queue growth.

sam_runtime: notes from config review: autoscaler headroom was set to 0.15 (15%) which for rapid bursts underestimates required ramp; also min_replicas small (2) for this customer's 100 RPS baseline. Their burst policy is not enabled (prewarm=false).

marta_support: customer also reported intermittent 401s when retrying during the spike — looks like a separate auth token refresh race under high load. We'll file a follow-up.

alex_infra: immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily bump customer's min_replicas to 8 for the campaign window (can do now, low risk), 2) enable prewarm for their route so we keep a warm pool (opsbot note: prewarm toggle applied to route acme/marketing at 1787654360), 3) open support ticket with cloud cp quota team to get sustained provisioning headroom.

devon_oncall: long-term: change scaler to consider pending_provision_count + queue_length (avoid waiting for arriving nodes). Also reduce probe timeouts so new instances join traffic faster and tune image caching (pull-through) to cut NotReady time.

sam_runtime: reproduced locally with the burst script; when we force a synthetic provision delay of ~60s we see the same 429 pattern. Attached short logs:
```
2025-11-03T21:04:02Z scaler: queue=320 threshold=150 -> scaling request x6
2025-11-03T21:04:05Z infra: provision_request_id=prov-9 rate_limited=1 retry_after=28s
2025-11-03T21:04:37Z infra: provision_request_id=prov-9 accepted
2025-11-03T21:05:18Z node prov-9 becomes Ready
2025-11-03T21:05:22Z router: backlog drained, 429 spike ended
```

lia_csm: customer wants a postmortem and a timeline. Can we confirm ETA for the min_replicas bump and prewarm config?

marta_support: min_replicas bumped to 8 at 1787654380, prewarm enabled at 1787654360. I've messaged the customer with interim update.

alex_infra: I've opened internal ticket INFRA-4821 with cloud quota team and linked the provision_request logs. Owner @alex_infra ETA 48h for quota clearance or emergency exception.

devon_oncall: action items: sam -> prototype scaler change (consider pending_provision_count) and shorter probe window (ETA 3d). alex -> follow quota. marta -> confirm customer campaign schedule and keep them updated. lia -> collect SLA docs.

sam_runtime: quick note: for immediate safety we should add an autoscaler policy override for customers flagged as "burst-critical" so their headroom is set to 30% and prewarm forced. I'll put a draft PR.

marta_support: thanks all — flagged as high priority for the customer. closing thread when we have postmortem and remediation plan. :thumbsup:
